subject: Pilot readiness KPI scorecard + Close playbook
messages:
From: Eliot Stevens <eliot@clearwell.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Cole <h.cole@clearwell.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot KPIs + proposed close path

Hi Grace / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We discussed a short pilot (6 weeks) to validate latency, accuracy on our triage prompts, and integration reliability. To move toward procurement we need a concise MAP that lists: success metrics, the explicit exit gates (what would make us stop), and the acceptance tests we’ll run at the end of the pilot.

I attached our internal template (pilot_kpi_template.xlsx) and a short list of procurement questions. High level asks from Clearwell:
- Average token-level latency target for triage flows (we care about p95 for live traffic)
- Quality threshold: automated QA checks + human review pass rate for clinical triage answers
- Data handling evidence (SOC2 excerpts / logging cadence)
- Cutover checklist and final sign-off process

Can you send back a MAP draft with the tests we should run (including a sample dataset and pass/fail thresholds) and a timeline for close? We’d like to align on the criteria before we loop in procurement.

Attachments: pilot_kpi_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Eliot
Eliot Stevens
Head of Product, Clearwell Health
eliot@clearwell.ai
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Eliot Stevens <eliot@clearwell.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot KPIs + proposed close path

Eliot —

Appreciate the clear ask. Draft MAP attached (MAP-final-draft.docx) — below is the condensed scorecard and the acceptance tests we propose for the 6-week pilot. If this looks right, we’ll update the spreadsheet and DocuSign the mutual action plan so procurement has a single source of truth.

Pilot readiness KPI scorecard (pass thresholds):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 400ms on production-simulated traffic (sample trace attached)
- Throughput: sustained 60 requests/min with 95% success under dedicated instance profile
- Accuracy / quality: automated eval on 1,000 labeled prompts: F1 >= 0.86 OR human review pass rate >= 92% across a 200-case random audit
- Safety/regulatory: zero high-severity PII leakage incidents in 6-week window; logging retained for 90 days and accessible via customer audit logs

Exit gates (stop or re-scope if any of these occur):
- Reproducible P95 latency > 700ms after tuning and one autoscaling cycle
- Human review pass rate < 80% after two remediation sprints
- Evidence of data exfiltration or inability to meet KMS/HSM key controls

Acceptance test suite (end of pilot):
1) Performance smoke: run 30-minute burst test using Clearwell traffic trace; verify p95 and error rate
2) Quality eval: run the 1,000-sample automated eval; sample 200 cases for human audit. Report confusion clusters and top 3 failure modes.
3) Integration resilience: execute failover injection (region switch) and confirm request routing and caching behavior preserved
4) Security evidence: provide SOC2 extract + audit log export (redacted) and confirm retention policy via console

Timeline / close path:
- Week 0: Kickoff + data exchange (sample set + access)
- Week 1–2: Integration and baseline runs; initial tuning
- Week 3–4: Full evaluation runs (automated + manual audits)
- Week 5: Remediation sprint if needed; compile findings
- Week 6: Acceptance run + mutual signoff; procurement handoff

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: will lead the evaluation runs and quality analysis (see tasks below)
- Ben: will schedule the baseline perf runs in Dedicated env and prepare the 30-min burst test config

I’ll push the MAP to the Google Sheet and link it to the HubSpot deal (RDW-4521). If you confirm the thresholds above I’ll convert to a DocuSign-ready MAP.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Attachments: MAP-final-draft.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Eliot Stevens <eliot@clearwell.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot KPIs + proposed close path

Looping in details / internal owners. Short notes / action items from our side:

- Security evidence: I attached a redacted SOC2 extract (SOC2-extract-redacted.pdf). Ben, can you confirm we can produce the audit-log export in the format Clearwell requested (CSV w/ request_id, timestamp, route, model_version)?
- Performance runbook: Ben, please configure the Dedicated pool with the suggested instance profile and validate p95 <= 400ms on the supplied trace. If we hit between 400–700ms after one tuning pass we surface remediation items; above 700ms we escalate to infra.
- Quality tooling: I’ll run the automated eval and deliver the labeled 1,000-sample report by end of week 4. For human review sampling, we’ll use the 200-case randomization in the attached spreadsheet.

Acceptance gating rubric (internal):
- Green: all KPIs meet thresholds. Signoff by Grace + Clearwell product lead.
- Yellow: any single KPI in the warning band (latency 400–700ms or human review 80–92%). Requires a documented remediation plan and a single-week extension to pilot.
- Red: any KPI in failure band (latency >700ms or human review <80% or security incident). Abort pilot and pause procurement.

Ben — action: schedule perf runs (week 1 & week 5) and capture detailed traces. I’ll own the eval scripts and the quality report. Grace: I’ll prepare the DocuSign-ready MAP once Eli confirms thresholds.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Grace / Marissa —

This looks good and aligns with how we wanted to structure the pilot. We approve the KPI thresholds and the acceptance test suite as outlined. A couple quick clarifications before DocuSign:
1) We agree to the yellow-window extension (one additional week) as the remediation path.
2) For the human audit, we’ll provide two clinician reviewers on our side; Redwood should provide the tooling export for sampling and annotation.
3) Procurement will need the final MAP in DocuSign format and the SOC2 redaction confirmation. I am copying Hannah from procurement to coordinate signature.

Please proceed to convert to DocuSign and share the Google Sheet link (I can see the draft at the link you mentioned).

Thanks,
Eliot
